gaps.text: In-line measurement of Melt temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor at the measurement point

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (MIR-ATR and Raman spectra are taken from one combined probe head at the same small melt volume, then normalised to a common time step and block-scaled before joining, because variables from different methods are not equivalent. Each block keeps its own calibration and diagnostics. The fused model must beat the better single method on held-out runs or batches, otherwise the extra instrument is dropped.)
Probe and fiber temperature ratings for a hot polymer melt interface.
Cleaning or anti-fouling measures for a build-up-prone measurement point.

items.finding: The source states that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the assessment by highlighting that temperature at the measurement point may need to be controlled or monitored when using MIR or NIR, and that temperature variation should be tested for its effect on spectra.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns aqueous solutions and NIR/MIR, not a hot polymer melt, and it does not describe an in-line temperature sensor or probe/fiber temperature rating.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The source warns that in some situations instrument complementarity, rather than data complementarity, was not sufficient to improve the performance of several predictive CQAs, citing a Raman and FT-IR food analytical study.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing whether a fused MIR-ATR and Raman model actually beats the better single method on held-out runs or batches before keeping the extra instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited case is a food analytical study using Raman and FT-IR, not MIR-ATR and Raman from one combined probe head in a hot polymer melt, so the outcome may not transfer.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36

items.finding: In one study, a signal-to-noise weighted NIR-MIR-Raman model showed the best performance compared with both combined and individual models, with a root mean square error of cross-validation of 0.75 Pa s and an RPD of 10.62.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform a comparison plan by suggesting that signal-to-noise weighting of blocks be tested and that the fused model be compared against the better single method.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study concerns micellar liquids and viscosity prediction, is available only as an abstract, and does not use the same combined probe head or hot polymer melt matrix.

citation.quote: The signal-to-noise weighted NIR-MIR-Raman model showed the best performance compared with both combined and individual models with a root mean square error of cross-validation of 0.75 Pa s and an RPD of 10.62.
citation.label: E04 ¶1
